summary: Kathryn R. Blackstone worked in Buddhist and religious studies. She held posts at Victoria University of Wellington and at the University of Manitoba (attested 1999).

Katia Buffetrille works in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Paris Nanterre University, studying under Alexander W. Macdonald, and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2000) and CRCAO.

Katragadda Paddayya is a scholar of archaeology and Indology. He earned his doctorate at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1963–1968) and served as a professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1970–2008).

Katsuhiko Kamimura was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Madras under Minoru Hara and V. Raghavan. He taught at Kokugakuin University and the University of Tokyo, including its Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.
Katsuhiro Yoshizawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University and served as a professor at Hanazono University.

Katsuji Fujioka was a linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1897) and the University of Leipzig (1901–1905). He served as an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo from 1910 to 1933.
Katsumi Kuroita was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896) and held a post there from around 1901 to 1935.

Katsumi Mimaki specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama and Hisashi Sato, and at Paris universities. He served as a professor at Kyoto University (1996–2010) and joined the Japan Academy.

Katsumi Okimoto was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who completed graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1973). He served as a professor (~1986–2009) and director (~2009–2014) at Hanazono University.

Katsumi Tanabe is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1961–1968) and held posts at Kanazawa University (~1993–1999) and Chuo University (~1999–2011).

Katsutoshi Ono was an archaeologist, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from Kyoto University. He worked at the Academy of Oriental Culture, Kyoto University, Nara National Museum, and as a professor at Ryukoku University.

Kavita Singh was an art historian and Indologist who studied at MSU Baroda and Panjab University. She was dean at the School of Arts and Aesthetics at Jawaharlal Nehru University, which she founded, and held posts at Marg Publications and SDMA.

Kazi Dawa Samdup worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying at Bhutia Boarding School under Ugyen Gyatso and Lopen Tshampa Norbu. He served as headmaster of Maharaja's Bhutia Boarding School (~1906–1919) and lecturer at the University of Calcutta (1920).

Kazu Uehara was an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyushu University (~1948–1992). He taught as a lecturer at the University of Miyazaki (~1954–1968) and served as professor emeritus at Seijo University (~1968–1995).

Kazuaki Komine specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate from Waseda University and held posts at Tokushima University, the National Institute of Japanese Literature, and Rikkyo University, where he became professor emeritus (1995–2013).

Kazuaki Tanahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Soichi Nakamura. He served as scholar in residence at the San Francisco Zen Center (1977–1984) and is a fellow of the World Academy of Art and Science.

Kazufumi Oki works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University and served as an associate professor (attested 1982–1990) and professor emeritus (attested 2006–2013) at Shuchiin University.

Kazuharu Mizuno studied at Nagoya University, Hokkaido University, and Tokyo Metropolitan University (DSc). He served as professor of geography in the Graduate School of Letters at Kyoto University (~2008–2024).

Kazuhiko Atsumi worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1954) and held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1960–1989) and Suzuka University of Medical Science (~1991–1998).

Kazuhiko Yoshida studied at Sophia University, Kyoto University, Osaka University, and under Jay Jasanoff at Cornell University (PhD). He served as an associate professor at Nagoya City College for Women and professor at Kyoto University (~1999–2020).
